rows.zh: 大多数人似乎在夜晚早些时候做更多噩梦，临近醒来时逐渐转向更愉快的梦，这表明他们正在化解白天产生的负面情绪。

rows.s: Because our conscious mind is occupied with daily life we don't always think about the emotional significance of the day's events—until, it appears, we begin to dream.
rows.zh: 由于我们的意识被日常生活所占据，我们并不总是会去思考当天事件的情感意义——直到，看起来，我们开始做梦的时候。

rows.s: And this process need not be left to the unconscious.
rows.zh: 而且这一过程不必完全交由潜意识来处理。

rows.s: Cartwright believes one can exercise conscious control over recurring bad dreams.
rows.zh: 卡特赖特相信，人能够对反复出现的噩梦施加有意识的控制。

rows.s: As soon as you awaken, identify what is upsetting about the dream.
rows.zh: 你一醒来，就辨明梦中究竟是什么令人不安。

rows.s: With much practice people can learn to, literally, do it in their sleep.
rows.zh: 经过大量练习，人们就能学会真正在睡梦中做到这一点。

rows.s: In dreams, a window opens into a world where logic is suspended and dead people speak.
rows.zh: 在梦中，一扇窗户开向一个逻辑被搁置、死者也能开口说话的世界。

rows.s: Terrorism, economic uncertainties and general feelings of insecurity have increased people's anxiety.
rows.zh: 恐怖主义、经济上的不确定性以及普遍的不安全感，加剧了人们的焦虑。

rows.s: Those suffering from persistent nightmares should seek help from a therapist.
rows.zh: 那些饱受持续噩梦折磨的人，应当向治疗师寻求帮助。

rows.s: For the rest of us, the brain has its ways of working through bad feelings.
rows.zh: 对我们其余的人来说，大脑自有它化解不良情绪的办法。

rows.s: Sleep—or rather dream—on it and you'll feel better in the morning.
rows.zh: 对它好好睡一觉——或者说，好好做个梦——你第二天早上就会感觉好些。

rows.s: A century ago, Freud formulated his revolutionary theory that dreams were the disguised shadows of our unconscious desires and fears; by the late 1970 s, neurologists had switched to thinking of them as just "mental noise"—the random byproducts of the neural-repair work that goes on during sleep.
rows.zh: 一个世纪前，弗洛伊德提出了他革命性的理论，认为梦是我们潜意识欲望和恐惧的伪装影像；而到了20世纪70年代末，神经学家已转而把梦仅仅看作"精神噪音"——即睡眠期间进行的神经修复工作的随机副产品。

rows.s: Now researchers suspect that dreams are part of the mind's emotional thermostat, regulating moods while the brain is "off-line."
rows.zh: 如今研究者怀疑，梦是大脑情绪调节器的一部分，在大脑"离线"时负责调节情绪。

rows.s: And one leading authority says that these intensely powerful mental events can be not only harnessed but actually brought under conscious control, to help us sleep and feel better.
rows.zh: 一位权威人士说，这些极其强烈的心理活动不仅能被驾驭，而且实际上能被纳入有意识的控制之下，从而帮助我们睡得更好、感觉更好。

rows.s: "It's your dream," says Rosalind Cartwright, chair of psychology at Chicago's Medical Center.
rows.zh: "这是你的梦，"芝加哥医学中心心理学系主任罗莎琳德·卡特赖特说。

rows.s: "If you don't like it, change it."
rows.zh: "如果你不喜欢它，就改变它。"

rows.s: Evidence from brain imaging supports this view.
rows.zh: 来自脑成像的证据支持这一观点。

rows.s: The brain is as active during REM (rapid eye movement) sleep—when most vivid dreams occur—as it is when fully awake, says Dr. Eric Nofzinger at the University of Pittsburgh.
rows.zh: 匹兹堡大学的埃里克·诺夫辛格博士说，大脑在快速眼动（REM）睡眠期间——也就是最生动的梦境出现之时——和它完全清醒时一样活跃。

rows.s: At the end of the day, there's probably little reason to pay attention to our dreams at all unless they keep us from sleeping or "we wake up in a panic," Cartwright says.
rows.zh: 归根结底，我们大概没什么理由去理会自己的梦——除非梦让我们无法入睡，或者"我们在惊恐中醒来"，卡特赖特说。

rows.s: Equally, in poetry, the highly personal, performative genre is the only form that could claim real liveliness.
rows.zh: 同样，在诗歌方面，高度个人化、表演性的体裁是唯一能够称得上真正富有生气的形式。

rows.s: In both oral and written English, talking is triumphing over speaking, spontaneity over craft.
rows.zh: 在口语和书面英语中，随意交谈正在压倒正式言说，自发性正在压倒技艺。

rows.s: Americans no longer expect public figures, whether in speech or in writing, to command the English language with skill and gift.
rows.zh: 美国人不再指望公众人物——无论是口头表达还是书面写作——能熟练而有天赋地驾驭英语。

rows.s: As a linguist, he acknowledges that all varieties of human language, including non-standard ones like Black English, can be powerfully expressive—there exists no language or dialect in the world that cannot convey complex ideas.
rows.zh: 作为一名语言学家，他承认人类语言的所有变体——包括像黑人英语这样的非标准变体——都能极富表现力：世界上不存在任何不能表达复杂思想的语言或方言。

rows.s: He is not arguing, as many do, that we can no longer think straight because we do not talk proper.
rows.zh: 他并不像许多人那样论证说：我们因为说话不规范，就再也不能清晰地思考了。

rows.s: Russians have a deep love for their own language and carry large chunks of memorized poetry in their heads, while Italian politicians tend to elaborate speech that would seem old-fashioned to most English-speakers.
rows.zh: 俄罗斯人深爱自己的语言，并在头脑中记诵着大段大段的诗歌，而意大利政客则倾向于精心雕琢的言辞——这在大多数说英语的人看来会显得过时。

rows.s: Mr. McWhorter acknowledges that formal language is not strictly necessary, and proposes no radical education reforms—he is really grieving over the loss of something beautiful more than useful.
rows.zh: 麦克沃特先生承认正式语言并非绝对必要，也没有提出任何激进的教育改革方案——他其实是在哀叹某种美好而非实用之物的失去。

rows.s: We now take our English "on paper plates instead of china".
rows.zh: 如今我们"用纸盘子而非瓷器"来享用英语。

rows.s: A shame, perhaps, but probably an inevitable one.
rows.zh: 这也许是一件憾事，但很可能是一件不可避免的憾事。

rows.s: Nor do they aspire to such command themselves.
rows.zh: 他们自己也不渴望拥有这样的语言驾驭能力。

rows.s: In his latest book, Doing Our Own Thing: The Degradation of language and Music and Why We Should, Like, Care, John McWhorter, a linguist and controversialist of mixed liberal and conservative views, sees the triumph of 1960s counter-culture as responsible for the decline of formal English.
rows.zh: 在他的新书《做我们自己的事：语言和音乐的退化以及我们为什么应该，嗯，在意》中，约翰·麦克沃特——一位兼具自由派与保守派观点的语言学家兼好辩之士——认为，20世纪60年代反主流文化的胜利应为正式英语的衰落负责。

rows.s: Blaming the permissive 1960s is nothing new, but this is not yet another criticism against the decline in education.
rows.zh: 指责放任的20世纪60年代并不是什么新鲜事，但这并非又一篇针对教育衰退的批评文章。

rows.s: Illustrated with an entertaining array of examples from both high and low culture, the trend that Mr. McWhorter documents is unmistakable.
rows.zh: 在用一系列来自高雅文化和通俗文化的有趣例子加以说明之后，麦克沃特先生所记录的这一趋势便显而易见了。

rows.s: Mr. McWhorter's academic speciality is language history and change, and he sees the gradual disappearance of "whom", for example, to be natural and no more regrettable than the loss of the case-endings of Old English.
rows.zh: 麦克沃特先生的学术专长是语言史与语言变迁，他认为，比如"whom"一词的逐渐消失是自然现象，并不比古英语格尾的丧失更令人惋惜。

rows.s: But the cult of the authentic and the personal, "doing our own thing", has spelt the death of formal speech, writing, poetry and music.
rows.zh: 然而，对本真与个性的崇拜，即"做我们自己的事"，已宣告了正式言说、写作、诗歌和音乐的终结。

rows.s: But it is less clear, to take the question of his subtitle, why we should, like, care.
rows.zh: 但是，就他副标题所提的问题而言，我们为什么应该，嗯，在意，这一点就不那么清楚了。

rows.s: While even the modestly educated sought an elevated tone when they put pen to paper before the 1960 s, even the most well regarded writing since then has sought to capture spoken English on the page.
rows.zh: 尽管在20世纪60年代之前，即便受教育程度一般的人提笔写作时也追求一种典雅的格调，但此后即便是最受推崇的写作也力图在纸面上捕捉口语化的英语。

rows.s: "On the day after we send our messages, we see a sharp increase in our traffic," says Seth Peets, vice president of marketing for CareerSite.
rows.zh: “在我们发送消息后的第二天，我们的网站流量会大幅增加，”CareerSite营销副总裁塞思·皮茨说道。

rows.s: With thousands of career-related sites on the Internet, finding promising openings can be time-consuming and inefficient.
rows.zh: 由于互联网上有数以千计的求职相关网站，寻找有希望的职位空缺可能既费时又低效。

rows.s: Instead, the best strategy is to use the agent as a kind of tip service to keep abreast of jobs in a particular database; when you get E-mail, consider it a reminder to check the database again.
rows.zh: 相反，最好的策略是把代理用作一种随时了解某个特定数据库中职位的工具；当你收到邮件时，就把它看作再次查看数据库的提醒。

rows.s: Narrowing your criteria, for example, may work against you: "Every time you answer a question you eliminate a possibility," says one expert.
rows.zh: 例如，缩小你的搜索条件可能对你不利：“每当你回答一个问题，你就排除了一种可能性，”一位专家说道。

rows.s: But although a search agent worked for Redmon, career experts see drawbacks.
rows.zh: 但是，尽管搜索代理对雷德蒙起了作用，职业专家们却看到了其中的弊端。

rows.s: Search agents reduce the need for repeated visits to the databases.
rows.zh: 搜索代理减少了反复访问数据库的需要。

rows.s: "I struck gold," says Redmon, who E-mailed his resume to the employer and won a position as in-house counsel for a company.
rows.zh: “我挖到了金子，”雷德蒙说道，他把简历用电子邮件发给了雇主，并获得了一家公司内部法律顾问的职位。

rows.s: Redmon chose the keywords legal, intellectual property and Washington, D.C. Three weeks later, he got his first notification of an opening.
rows.zh: 雷德蒙选定了关键词：法律、知识产权和华盛顿特区。三周后，他收到了第一份职位空缺通知。

rows.s: It's an interactive feature that lets visitors key in job criteria such as location, title, and salary, then E-mails them when a matching position is posted in the database.
rows.zh: 它是一项互动功能，让访问者输入诸如地点、职位和薪水等求职条件，然后在数据库中出现匹配职位时给他们发送邮件。

rows.s: Working with a personal search agent means having another set of eyes looking out for you.
rows.zh: 使用个人搜索代理意味着多了一双替你留意的眼睛。

rows.s: "You always keep your eyes open," he says.
rows.zh: “你总得保持警觉，”他说道。

rows.s: Although happily employed, Redmon maintains his agent at CareerBuilder.
rows.zh: 尽管雷德蒙已经愉快地就业，他仍保留着自己在CareerBuilder上的代理。

rows.s: Some use them to keep a close watch on the demand for their line of work or gather information on compensation to arm themselves when negotiating for a raise.
rows.zh: 有些人用它们密切关注本行业的需求，或收集薪酬信息，以便在谈判加薪时为自己增添筹码。

rows.s: He searched it with no success but was attracted by the site's "personal search agent".
rows.zh: 他搜索了一番却一无所获，但被该网站的“个人搜索代理”功能所吸引。

rows.s: Even those who aren't hunting for jobs may find search agents worthwhile.
rows.zh: 即使是那些并非在找工作的人，也可能发现搜索代理很有价值。

rows.s: There may be more matches in the database; job hunters will have to visit the site again to find them—and they do.
rows.zh: 数据库里可能有更多匹配信息；求职者将不得不再次访问该网站去找到它们——而他们也的确这么做了。

rows.s: When CareerSite's agent sends out messages to those who have signed up for its service, for example, it includes only three potential jobs—those it considers the best matches.
rows.zh: 例如，当CareerSite的代理向那些注册了其服务的人发送消息时，它只包含三个潜在的职位——即它认为最匹配的那几个。

rows.s: Some sites design their agents to tempt job hunters to return.
rows.zh: 一些网站把它们的代理设计成引诱求职者再次访问的工具。

rows.s: "I would not rely on agents for finding everything that is added to a database that might interest me," says the author of a job-searching guide.
rows.zh: “我不会依靠代理来查找所有被添加到某个可能令我感兴趣的数据库中的东西，”一本求职指南的作者说道。

rows.s: "There's no career counseling implicit in all of this."
rows.zh: “这一切当中并不隐含任何职业咨询。”

rows.s: "None of these programs do that," says another expert.
rows.zh: “这些程序没有一个能做到这一点，”另一位专家说道。

rows.s: For any job search, you should start with a narrow concept—what you think you want to do—then broaden it.
rows.zh: 对于任何求职，你都应该从一个狭窄的概念入手——即你认为自己想做的事——然后再加以拓展。

rows.s: Hunting for a job late last year, lawyer Gant Redmon stumbled across CareerBuilder, a job database on the Internet.
rows.zh: 去年年底找工作时，律师甘特·雷德蒙偶然发现了CareerBuilder——一个网上的求职数据库。

rows.s: One theory, dreamt up in all the spare time enjoyed by the alphabetically disadvantaged, is that the rot sets in early.
rows.zh: 有一种理论是那些在字母上处于不利地位的人利用其全部空闲时间凭空想出来的，它认为这种弊病在很早的时候就已经埋下了。

rows.s: Can this merely be coincidence?
rows.zh: 这难道仅仅是巧合吗？

rows.s: As are the world's five richest men (Gates, Buffett, Allen, Ellison and Albrecht).
rows.zh: 世界五大富豪（盖茨、巴菲特、艾伦、埃里森和阿尔布雷希特）同样如此。

rows.s: The world's three top central bankers (Greenspan, Duisenberg and Hayami) are all close to the top of the alphabet, even if one of them really uses Japanese characters.
rows.zh: 世界三大顶尖央行行长（格林斯潘、杜伊森贝赫和速水）都接近字母表的顶端，即便他们当中有一位实际上使用的是日文字符。

rows.s: Over the past century, all kinds of unfairness and discrimination have been condemned or made illegal.
rows.zh: 在过去的一个世纪里，各种各样的不公平和歧视都已遭到谴责或被宣布为非法。

rows.s: This, for those as yet unaware of such a disadvantage, refers to discrimination against those whose surnames begin with a letter in the lower half of the alphabet.
rows.zh: 对于那些尚未意识到这种不利处境的人来说，这指的是针对姓氏以字母表后半部分字母开头的人的歧视。

rows.s: It has long been known that a taxi firm called AAAA cars has a big advantage over Zodiac cars when customers thumb through their phone directories.
rows.zh: 人们早就知道，当顾客翻查电话簿时，一家名为AAAA的出租车公司比Zodiac出租车公司具有很大的优势。

rows.s: Less well known is the advantage that Adam Abbott has in life over Zoë Zysman.
rows.zh: 更鲜为人知的是亚当·阿伯特在人生中相对于佐伊·齐斯曼所拥有的那种优势。

rows.s: English names are fairly evenly spread between the halves of the alphabet.
rows.zh: 英文名字在字母表的前后两半之间分布得相当均匀。

rows.s: Yet a suspiciously large number of top people have surnames beginning with letters between A and K.
rows.zh: 然而，数量大得可疑的高层人物，其姓氏都以A到K之间的字母开头。

rows.s: Thus the American president and vice-president have surnames starting with B and C respectively; and 26 of George Bush's predecessors (including his father) had surnames in the first half of the alphabet against just 16 in the second half.
rows.zh: 因此，美国总统和副总统的姓氏分别以B和C开头；乔治·布什的前任中（包括他的父亲）有26位姓氏处于字母表前半部分，而处于后半部分的仅有16位。

rows.s: So short-sighted Zysman junior gets stuck in the back row, and is rarely asked the improving questions posed by those insensitive teachers.
rows.zh: 于是，近视的小齐斯曼被困在后排，也很少被那些麻木不仁的老师提问那些能让人进步的问题。

rows.s: At the time the alphabetically disadvantaged may think they have had a lucky escape.
rows.zh: 在当时，那些字母上处于不利地位的人可能会以为自己幸运地逃过了一劫。

rows.s: Yet the result may be worse qualifications, because they get less individual attention, as well as less confidence in speaking publicly.
rows.zh: 然而，其结果可能是较差的资历，因为他们得到的个别关注较少，当众讲话的自信也较低。

rows.s: At university graduation ceremonies, the ABCs proudly get their awards first; by the time they reach the Zysmans most people are literally having a ZZZ.
rows.zh: 在大学毕业典礼上，姓氏以ABC开头的人骄傲地最先领取奖项；而等到轮到齐斯曼这类人时……

rows.s: Even more striking, six of the seven heads of government of the G 7 rich countries are alphabetically advantaged (Berlusconi, Blair, Bush, Chirac, Chrétien and Koizumi).
rows.zh: 更引人注目的是，七国集团富裕国家的七位政府首脑中有六位在字母上占优（贝卢斯科尼、布莱尔、布什、希拉克、克雷蒂安和小泉）。

rows.s: The humiliation continues.
rows.zh: 这种羞辱还在继续。

rows.s: At the start of the first year in infant school, teachers seat pupils alphabetically from the front, to make it easier to remember their names.
rows.zh: 在幼儿学校第一学年开始时，老师们按字母顺序从前排开始给学生排座位，以便更容易记住他们的名字。

rows.s: But one insidious form continues to thrive: alphabetism.
rows.zh: 但有一种隐蔽的形式仍在盛行，那就是字母歧视。

rows.s: Shortlists for job interviews, election ballot papers, lists of conference speakers and attendees: all tend to be drawn up alphabetically, and their recipients lose interest as they plough through them.
rows.zh: 求职面试的候选名单、选举投票单、会议发言者及与会者名单——所有这些往往都按字母顺序拟定，而收到这些名单的人在费力地从头看到尾的过程中会逐渐失去兴趣。

rows.s: Many consumers seem to have been influenced by stock-market swings, which investors now view as a necessary ingredient to a sustained boom.
rows.zh: 许多消费者似乎受到了股市波动的影响，而如今投资者将这种波动视为经济持续繁荣所不可或缺的要素。

rows.s: In Manhattan, "there's a new gold rush happening in the $4 million to $10 million range, predominantly fed by Wall Street bonuses," says broker Barbara Corcoran.
rows.zh: 经纪人芭芭拉·科克伦说，在曼哈顿，“正出现一波新的淘金热，主要是由华尔街的奖金所助推。”

rows.s: When it comes to the slowing economy, Ellen Spero isn't biting her nails just yet.
rows.zh: 说到正在放缓的经济，……

rows.s: From car dealerships to Gap outlets, sales have been lagging for months as shoppers temper their spending.
rows.zh: 从汽车经销店到盖璞专卖店，由于购物者纷纷节制开支，销售已连续数月低迷。

rows.s: For retailers, who last year took in 24 percent of their revenue between Thanksgiving and Christmas, the cautious approach is coming at a crucial time.
rows.zh: 对零售商而言——他们去年在感恩节至圣诞节期间获得了全年收入的24%——这种谨慎的消费心态出现在一个关键的时刻。

rows.s: Already, experts say, holiday sales are off 7 percent from last year's pace.
rows.zh: 专家称，目前节日销售额已比去年同期下降了7%。

rows.s: But don't sound any alarms just yet.
rows.zh: 但先别急着拉响警报。

rows.s: Consumers seem only mildly concerned, not panicked, and many say they remain optimistic about the economy's long-term prospects even as they do some modest belt-tightening.
rows.zh: 消费者似乎只是略有担忧，而非惊慌失措；许多人表示，尽管他们正在适度地勒紧裤腰带，但仍对经济的长期前景保持乐观。

rows.s: Consumers say they're not in despair because, despite the dreadful headlines, their own fortunes still feel pretty good.
rows.zh: 消费者说他们并不绝望，因为尽管头条新闻令人不安，但他们自身的财务状况依然让人感觉相当不错。

rows.s: Home prices are holding steady in most regions.
rows.zh: 在大多数地区，房价保持平稳。

rows.s: In San Francisco, prices are still rising even as frenzied overbidding quiets.
rows.zh: 在旧金山，尽管疯狂的竞相加价已趋平静，房价仍在上涨。

rows.s: "Instead of 20 to 30 offers, now maybe you only get two or three," says John Tealdi, a Bay Area real-estate broker.
rows.zh: “过去会有20到30个报价，现在也许你只能收到两三个，”湾区房地产经纪人约翰·特尔迪说。

rows.s: Getting a table at Manhattan's hot new Alain Ducasse restaurant used to be impossible. Not anymore.
rows.zh: 过去，要在曼哈顿炙手可热的新餐厅阿兰·杜卡斯订到一张桌子几乎是不可能的。如今不再如此。

rows.s: But the 47-year-old manicurist isn't cutting, filing or polishing as many nails as she'd like to, either.
rows.zh: 但这位47岁的修甲师如今也没能像她希望的那样修剪、锉磨或打磨那么多的指甲。

rows.s: And most folks still feel pretty comfortable about their ability to find and keep a job.
rows.zh: 而且大多数人对自己找到并保住一份工作的能力仍然感觉相当踏实。

rows.s: Many folks see silver linings to this slowdown.
rows.zh: 许多人在这次经济放缓中看到了一线希望。

rows.s: Potential home buyers would cheer for lower interest rates.
rows.zh: 潜在的购房者会为更低的利率而欢呼。

rows.s: Employers wouldn't mind a little fewer bubbles in the job market.
rows.zh: 雇主们也不会介意就业市场上的泡沫少一些。

rows.s: Diners might see an upside, too.
rows.zh: 外出就餐的人或许也能从中看到好处。

rows.s: For that, Greenspan & Co. may still be worth toasting.
rows.zh: 为此，格林斯潘及其同僚或许仍然值得人们为之举杯庆贺。

rows.s: Most of her clients spend $12 to $50 weekly, but last month two longtime customers suddenly stopped showing up.
rows.zh: 她的大多数客户每周花费12到50美元，但上个月有两位老顾客突然不再光顾了。

rows.s: Spero blames the softening economy.
rows.zh: 斯佩罗把这归咎于日渐疲软的经济。

rows.s: "I'm a good economic indicator," she says.
rows.zh: “我是个很好的经济晴雨表，”她说。

rows.s: "I provide a service that people can do without when they're concerned about saving some dollars."
rows.zh: “我提供的是一种当人们想省钱时可有可无的服务。”

rows.s: So Spero is downscaling, shopping at middle-brow Dillard's department store near her suburban Cleveland home, instead of Neiman Marcus.
rows.zh: 于是斯佩罗开始降低消费档次，去她克利夫兰郊区家附近那家档次居中的迪拉德百货购物，而不再光顾尼曼百货。

rows.s: "I don't know if other clients are going to abandon me, too," she says.
rows.zh: “我不知道其他客户是不是也会离我而去，”她说。

rows.s: Even before Alan Greenspan's admission that America's red-hot economy is cooling, lots of working folks had already seen signs of the slowdown themselves.
rows.zh: 甚至早在艾伦·格林斯潘承认美国炙手可热的经济正在降温之前，许多上班族自己就已经察觉到了经济放缓的迹象。

rows.s: Intelligence seeks to grasp, manipulate, re-order, and adjust, while intellect examines, ponders, wonders, theorizes, criticizes, and imagines.
rows.zh: 才智力求抓取、操控、重排和调整，而智识则审视、思考、好奇、构建理论、批判和想象。

rows.s: Intellect is the critical, creative, and contemplative side of the mind.
rows.zh: 智识是心智中批判的、创造的和沉思的那一面。

rows.s: Our heroes are athletes, entertainers, and entrepreneurs, not scholars.
rows.zh: 我们心目中的英雄是运动员、演艺人员和企业家，而不是学者。

rows.s: Intellect, according to Hofstadter, is different from native intelligence, a quality we reluctantly admire.
rows.zh: 按照霍夫施塔特的说法，智识不同于天生的才智，后者是一种我们勉强佩服的品质。

rows.s: Its hero avoids being civilized—going to school and learning to read—so he can preserve his innate goodness.
rows.zh: 书中的主人公拒绝被文明化——即拒绝上学和学习读书——这样他就能保持自己天生的善良。

rows.s: Ralph Waldo Emerson and other Transcendentalist philosophers thought schooling and rigorous book learning put unnatural restraints on children: "We are shut up in schools and college recitation rooms for 10 or 15 years and come out at last with a bellyful of words and do not know a thing."Mark Twain's Huckleberry Finn exemplified American anti-intellectualism.
rows.zh: 拉尔夫·沃尔多·爱默生和其他超验主义哲学家认为，学校教育和严格的书本学习给孩子施加了不自然的束缚：“我们被关在学校和大学的背诵课堂里十年或十五年，最后满腹辞藻地走出来，却什么都不懂。”马克·吐温笔下的哈克贝利·费恩正是美国反智主义的典型。

rows.s: We will have a less civil society."
rows.zh: 我们将拥有一个文明程度更低的社会。”

rows.s: Continuing along this path, says writer Earl Shorris, "We will become a second-rate country.
rows.zh: 作家厄尔·肖里斯说，沿着这条道路走下去，“我们将沦为一个二流国家。

rows.s: Without the ability to think critically, to defend their ideas and understand the ideas of others, they cannot fully participate in our democracy.
rows.zh: 如果不具备批判性思考、捍卫自己观点并理解他人观点的能力，他们就无法充分参与我们的民主。

rows.s: "Intellect is resented as a form of power or privilege," writes historian and professor Richard Hofstadter in Anti-intellectualism in American Life, a Pulitzer-Prize winning book on the roots of anti-intellectualism in US politics, religion, and education.
rows.zh: 历史学家兼教授理查德·霍夫施塔特在《美国生活中的反智主义》一书中写道：“智识被当作一种权力或特权而遭人忌恨。”该书荣获普利策奖，探讨了美国政治、宗教和教育中反智主义的根源。

rows.s: Encouraging kids to reject the life of the mind leaves them vulnerable to exploitation and control.
rows.zh: 鼓励孩子拒斥心智生活，会使他们易受剥削和操控。

rows.s: Americans today don't place a very high value on intellect.
rows.zh: 如今的美国人并不十分看重智识。

rows.s: Practicality, common sense, and native intelligence have been considered more noble qualities than anything you could learn from a book.
rows.zh: 务实、常识和天生才智一向被视为比你能从书本中学到的任何东西都更为高贵的品质。

rows.s: Left Back: A Century of Failed School Reforms, traces the roots of anti-intellectualism in our schools, concluding they are anything but a counterbalance to the American distaste for intellectual pursuits.
rows.zh: 《落在后面：一个世纪以来失败的学校改革》追溯了我们学校中反智主义的根源，并得出结论说：学校非但不是、反而绝非对美国人厌恶智识追求这一倾向的制衡。

rows.s: But they could and should be.
rows.zh: 但学校本可以、也理应成为这样的制衡力量。

rows.s: Ravitch's latest book.
rows.zh: 拉维奇的最新著作。

rows.s: "Schools could be a counterbalance."
rows.zh: “学校本可以成为一种制衡的力量。”

rows.s: From the beginning of our history, says Hofstadter, our democratic and populist urges have driven us to reject anything that smells of elitism.
rows.zh: 霍夫施塔特说，从我们历史伊始，我们的民主和民粹冲动就驱使我们拒斥任何带有精英主义气息的东西。

rows.s: "Schools have always been in a society where practical is more important than intellectual," says education writer Diane Ravitch.
rows.zh: 教育作家黛安·拉维奇说：“学校一向处在一个实用比智识更重要的社会之中。”

rows.s: Symptoms of pervasive anti-intellectualism in our schools aren't difficult to find.
rows.zh: 我们学校中普遍存在的反智主义的种种迹象不难发现。

rows.s: Even our schools are where we send our children to get a practical education—not to pursue knowledge for the sake of knowledge.
rows.zh: 就连我们的学校也成了把孩子送去接受实用教育的地方，而不是为求知本身而追求知识的地方。

rows.s: Hofstadter says our country's educational system is in the grips of people who "joyfully and militantly proclaim their hostility to intellect and their eagerness to identify with children who show the least intellectual promise."
rows.zh: 霍夫施塔特说，我们国家的教育体制掌握在这样一些人手中：他们兴高采烈而又咄咄逼人地宣示自己对智识的敌意，以及自己急于认同那些最缺乏智识潜质的孩子。

rows.s: School remains a place where intellect is mistrusted.
rows.zh: 学校仍然是一个智识不被信任的地方。

rows.s: Several of his staff members have military-intelligence backgrounds.
rows.zh: 他的几名员工拥有军事情报背景。

rows.s: In 1995 the CIA held a contest to see who could compile the most data about Burundi.
rows.zh: 1995年，中央情报局举办了一场比赛，看谁能收集到关于布隆迪最多的资料。

rows.s: The spooks call it "open source intelligence," and as the Net grows, it is becoming increasingly influential.
rows.zh: 间谍们把它称作“开源情报”，而且随着网络的发展，它正变得越来越有影响力。

rows.s: In the past three or four years, the World Wide Web has given birth to a whole industry of point-and-click spying.
rows.zh: 在过去的三四年里，万维网催生了一整个“点击即可”的间谍行业。

rows.s: That kind of electronic spying has been going on for decades.
rows.zh: 那种电子间谍活动已经存在几十年了。

rows.s: The latest revolution isn't simply a matter of gentlemen reading other gentlemen's e-mail.
rows.zh: 这场最新的革命不仅仅是绅士偷看其他绅士电子邮件那回事。

rows.s: Many of its predictions are available online at www.straitford.com.
rows.zh: 它的许多预测都可以在 www.straiford.com 网站上在线获取。

rows.s: The American spymaster who built the Office of Strategic Services in the World War II and later laid the roots for the CIA was fascinated with information.
rows.zh: 这位在二战期间创建了战略情报局、后来又为中央情报局奠定根基的美国间谍大师，对情报十分着迷。

rows.s: Among the firms making the biggest splash in the new world is Straitford, Inc., a private intelligence-analysis firm based in Austin, Texas.
rows.zh: 在新世界中引起最大轰动的公司当中，就有斯特拉特福公司，一家总部设在得克萨斯州奥斯汀的私营情报分析公司。

rows.s: Straitford president George Friedman says he sees the online world as a kind of mutually reinforcing tool for both information collection and distribution, a spymaster's dream.
rows.zh: 斯特拉特福公司总裁乔治·弗里德曼说，他把网络世界看作一种集信息收集与发布于一体、可相互强化的工具——一个间谍大师梦寐以求的工具。

rows.s: These days the Net, which has already re-made such everyday pastimes as buying books and sending mail, is reshaping Donovan's vocation as well.
rows.zh: 如今，已经重塑了买书、寄信等日常活动的互联网，也正在重塑多诺万所从事的那一行当。

rows.s: Donovan believed in using whatever tools came to hand in the "great game" of espionage—spying as a "profession."
rows.zh: 多诺万信奉在间谍这一“伟大游戏”——把间谍活动当作一种“职业”——中使用任何能到手的工具。

rows.s: Straitford, says Friedman, takes pride in its independent voice.
rows.zh: 弗里德曼说，斯特拉特福公司以其独立的声音而自豪。

rows.s: Straitford's briefs don't sound like the usual Washington back-and-forthing, whereby agencies avoid dramatic declarations on the chance they might be wrong.
rows.zh: 斯特拉特福公司的简报听起来不像华盛顿惯常的那种来回扯皮——在那种扯皮中，各机构因担心可能出错而回避做出引人注目的论断。

rows.s: He sees the firm's outsider status as the key to its success.
rows.zh: 他把公司的“局外人”身份视为其成功的关键。

rows.s: Friedman relies on a lean staff of 20 in Austin.
rows.zh: 弗里德曼依靠奥斯汀的一支20人的精干员工队伍。

rows.s: That's where Straitford earns its keep.
rows.zh: 而这正是斯特拉特福公司赚取报酬之所在。

rows.s: Open-source spying does have its risks, of course, since it can be difficult to tell good information from bad.
rows.zh: 当然，开源间谍活动确实有其风险，因为要把好情报和坏情报区分开可能很困难。

rows.s: "And we'll hear back from some of them."
rows.zh: “而且我们会收到他们当中一些人的回音。”

rows.s: "As soon as that report runs, we'll suddenly get 500 new internet sign-ups from Ukraine," says Friedman, a former political science professor.
rows.zh: “那份报告一发布，我们就会突然收到来自乌克兰的500个新的互联网注册，”身为前政治学教授的弗里德曼说。

rows.s: Last week his firm was busy vacuuming up data bits from the far corners of the world and predicting a crisis in Ukraine.
rows.zh: 上周，他的公司忙着从世界各个偏远角落搜集数据碎片，并预测乌克兰将爆发一场危机。

rows.s: Straitford makes money by selling the results of spying (covering nations from Chile to Russia) to corporations like energy-services firm McDermott International.
rows.zh: Straitford公司通过把间谍活动（范围涵盖从智利到俄罗斯的众多国家）的成果出售给像能源服务公司麦克德莫特国际这样的企业来赚钱。

rows.s: The winner, by a large margin, was a tiny Virginia company called Open-Source Solutions, whose clear advantage was its mastery of the electronic world.
rows.zh: 获胜者以巨大优势胜出，是弗吉尼亚一家名叫“开源解决方案”的小公司，其明显优势在于对电子世界的精通。

rows.s: Wild Bill Donovan would have loved the Internet.
rows.zh: 狂野比尔·多诺万会喜欢上互联网的。

rows.s: Asked what will happen when epidemics return, she said, "Don't worry, scientists will find some way of using computers."
rows.zh: 当被问及流行病卷土重来时会发生什么，她说：“别担心，科学家会找到使用计算机的某种办法。”

rows.s: To paraphrase 18th-century statesman Edmund Burke, "all that is needed for the triumph of a misguided cause is that good people do nothing."
rows.zh: 套用18世纪政治家埃德蒙·伯克的话说，一个被误导的事业取得成功所需要的，就是好人什么都不做。

rows.s: One such cause now seeks to end biomedical research because of the theory that animals have rights ruling out their use in research.
rows.zh: 如今，一个这样的事业正谋求终止生物医学研究，其依据是这样一种理论：动物拥有权利，从而排除了将其用于研究的可能。

rows.s: Hearing allegations of cruelty to animals in research settings, many are perplexed that anyone would deliberately harm an animal.
rows.zh: 当听到关于研究场所中虐待动物的指控时，许多人感到困惑：竟会有人故意伤害动物。

rows.s: Such well-meaning people just don't understand.
rows.zh: 这些好心人就是不明白。

rows.s: Scientists must communicate their message to the public in a compassionate, understandable way—in human terms, not in the language of molecular biology.
rows.zh: 科学家必须以一种富有同情心、易于理解的方式向公众传达他们的信息——用大众化的语言，而不是分子生物学的术语。

rows.s: We need to make clear the connection between animal research and a grandmother's hip replacement, a father's bypass operation, a baby's vaccinations, and even a pet's shots.
rows.zh: 我们需要讲清楚动物研究与祖母的髋关节置换、父亲的搭桥手术、婴儿的疫苗接种乃至宠物的打针之间的联系。

rows.s: To those who are unaware that animal research was needed to produce these treatments, as well as new treatments and vaccines, animal research seems wasteful at best and cruel at worst.
rows.zh: 对于那些不了解动物研究曾是制造这些治疗手段以及新的治疗手段和疫苗所必需的人来说，动物研究往好里说是浪费，往坏里说是残忍。

rows.s: They should be quick to respond to letters to the editor, lest animal rights misinformation go unchallenged and acquire a deceptive appearance of truth.
rows.zh: 他们应当迅速回应致编辑的信件，以免动物权利方面的错误信息无人质疑，进而获得貌似真理的欺骗性外表。

rows.s: Research institutions could be opened to tours, to show that laboratory animals receive humane care.
rows.zh: 研究机构可以开放供人参观，以表明实验动物受到人道的照料。

rows.s: When assured that they do, she replied, "Then I would have to say yes."
rows.zh: 当被告知确实如此时，她回答说：“那么我只好说是了。”

rows.s: Much can be done.
rows.zh: 可以做的事情有很多。

rows.s: Finally, because the ultimate stakeholders are patients, the health research community should actively recruit to its cause not only well-known personalities such as Stephen Cooper, who has made courageous statements about the value of animal research, but all who receive medical treatment.
rows.zh: 最后，由于最终的利益相关者是患者，健康研究界应当积极地为其事业招募人员，不仅包括像斯蒂芬·库珀这样曾就动物研究的价值发表过勇敢声明的知名人士，还包括所有接受医疗的人。

rows.s: Asked if she opposed immunizations, she wanted to know if vaccines come from animal research.
rows.zh: 当被问及是否反对免疫接种时，她想知道疫苗是否来自动物研究。

rows.s: Scientists could "adopt" middle school classes and present their own research.
rows.zh: 科学家可以“认领”中学班级，并展示他们自己的研究。

rows.s: If good people do nothing, there is a real possibility that an uninformed citizenry will extinguish the precious embers of medical progress.
rows.zh: 如果好人什么都不做，那么就真有可能出现这样一种情况：不明真相的公民将会熄灭医学进步的珍贵余烬。

rows.s: For example, a grandmotherly woman staffing an animal rights booth at a recent street fair was distributing a brochure that encouraged readers not to use anything that comes from or is tested in animals—no meat, no fur, no medicines.
rows.zh: 例如，在最近一次街头集市上，一位照看动物权利展位的慈祥老妇人正在散发一份小册子，鼓励读者不要使用任何源自动物或在动物身上做过试验的东西——不吃肉、不穿皮草、不用药品。

rows.s: Scientists need to respond forcefully to animal rights advocates, whose arguments are confusing the public and thereby threatening advances in health knowledge and care.
rows.zh: 科学家需要强有力地回应动物权利倡导者，这些人的论点正在使公众感到困惑，从而威胁到健康知识与护理方面的进步。

rows.s: Leaders of the animal rights movement target biomedical research because it depends on public funding, and few people understand the process of health care research.
rows.zh: 动物权利运动的领导者之所以把生物医学研究作为攻击目标，是因为它依赖公共资金，而且很少有人了解医疗保健研究的过程。

rows.s: Yet railroads continue to borrow billions to acquire one another, with Wall Street cheering them on.
rows.zh: 然而，铁路公司仍继续借入数十亿美元来相互收购，而华尔街还在一旁为它们助威。

rows.s: In recent years, railroads have been combining with each other, merging into supersystems, causing heightened concerns about monopoly.
rows.zh: 近年来，铁路公司一直在相互合并，组合成大型铁路系统，从而引发了人们对垄断的高度担忧。

rows.s: Railroads justify rate discrimination against captive shippers on the grounds that in the long run it reduces everyone's cost.
rows.zh: 铁路公司为针对受制托运人的费率歧视辩护，理由是从长远来看，这会降低所有人的成本。

rows.s: If railroads charged all customers the same average rate, they argue, shippers who have the option of switching to trucks or other forms of transportation would do so, leaving remaining customers to shoulder the cost of keeping up the line.
rows.zh: 他们辩称，如果铁路公司向所有客户收取相同的平均费率，那么可以选择改用卡车或其他运输方式的托运人便会这样做，从而让剩下的客户来承担维持线路的费用。

rows.s: It's theory to which many economists subscribe, but in practice it often leaves railroads in the position of determining which companies will flourish and which will fail.
rows.zh: 这是一种许多经济学家所赞同的理论，但在实践中它常常使铁路公司处于决定哪些公司兴盛、哪些公司倒闭的地位。

rows.s: Many captive shippers also worry they will soon be hit with a round of huge rate increases.
rows.zh: 许多受制托运人还担心，他们很快就会遭遇一轮大幅涨价。

rows.s: Consider the $10.2 billion bid by Norfolk Southern and CSX to acquire Conrail this year.
rows.zh: 请想想今年诺福克南方公司和CSX公司提出的以102亿美元收购康雷尔公司的出价。

rows.s: Conrail's net railway operating income in 1996 was just $427 million, less than half of the carrying costs of the transaction.
rows.zh: 康雷尔公司1996年的铁路营业净收入仅为4.27亿美元，还不到这笔交易承付成本的一半。

rows.s: Who's going to pay for the rest of the bill?
rows.zh: 那么，剩下的账单由谁来支付呢？

rows.s: As recently as 1995, the top four railroads accounted for under 70 percent of the total ton-miles moved by rails.
rows.zh: 就在1995年，排名前四的铁路公司占铁路运输总吨英里数的比例还不到70%。

rows.s: Many captive shippers fear that they will, as Norfolk Southern and CSX increase their grip on the market.
rows.zh: 许多受制托运人担心，随着诺福克南方公司和CSX公司加强对市场的控制，他们将不得不为此买单。

rows.s: Next year, after a series of mergers is completed, just four railroads will control well over 90 percent of all the freight moved by major rail carriers.
rows.zh: 明年，在一系列合并完成之后，仅四家铁路公司就将控制各大铁路运输公司所运送货运量的90%以上。

rows.s: Supporters of the new supersystems argue that these mergers will allow for substantial cost reductions and better coordinated service.
rows.zh: 新型大型铁路系统的支持者们认为，这些合并将能够大幅降低成本，并提供更为协调的服务。

rows.s: Any threat of monopoly, they argue, is removed by fierce competition from trucks.
rows.zh: 他们辩称，来自卡车运输的激烈竞争已经消除了任何垄断的威胁。

rows.s: But many shippers complain that for heavy bulk commodities traveling long distances, such as coal, chemicals, and grain, trucking is too costly and the railroads therefore have them by the throat.
rows.zh: 但许多托运人抱怨说，对于长途运输的大宗散装商品（如煤炭、化学品和谷物）来说，卡车运输成本太高，因此铁路公司便扼住了它们的咽喉。

rows.s: The vast consolidation within the rail industry means that most shippers are served by only one rail company.
rows.zh: 铁路行业内的大规模整合意味着，大多数托运人只能由一家铁路公司提供服务。

rows.s: Railroads typically charge such"captive"shippers 20 to 30 percent more than they do when another railroad is competing for the business.
rows.zh: 铁路公司向这类"受制"托运人收取的费用，要比有另一家铁路公司争夺这笔业务时高出20%到30%。

rows.s: Shippers who feel they are being overcharged have the right to appeal to the federal government's Surface Transportation Board for rate relief, but the process is expensive, time consuming, and will work only in truly extreme cases.
rows.zh: 认为自己被多收费的托运人有权向联邦政府的地面运输委员会申诉以求降价，但这一过程代价高昂、耗费时间，而且只在真正极端的情况下才管用。

rows.s: "Do we really want railroads to be the arbiters of who wins and who loses in the marketplace?" asks Martin Bercovici, a Washington lawyer who frequently represents shippers.
rows.zh: "我们真的希望铁路公司成为市场上谁输谁赢的裁决者吗？"经常代理托运人的华盛顿律师马丁·贝尔科维奇问道。

rows.s: The railroad industry as a whole, despite its brightening fortunes, still does not earn enough to cover the cost of the capital it must invest to keep up with its surging traffic.
rows.zh: 铁路行业作为一个整体，尽管前景日益好转，但其收入仍不足以支付为跟上激增运量而必须投入的资本成本。

rows.s: In 2002, the cost will be $1,540 billion.
rows.zh: 到2002年，这笔费用将达到15400亿美元。

rows.s: Anyone can see this trend is unsustainable.
rows.zh: 任何人都能看出这一趋势是不可持续的。

rows.s: Yet few seem willing to try to reverse it.
rows.zh: 然而似乎很少有人愿意去尝试扭转这一趋势。

rows.s: Some scholars conclude that a government with finite resources should simply stop paying for medical care that sustains life beyond a certain age—say 83 or so.
rows.zh: 一些学者得出结论：资源有限的政府应当干脆停止为那些将生命维持到某个年龄——比如说83岁左右——之后的医疗买单。

rows.s: In 1950, the US spent $12.7 billion on health care.
rows.zh: 1950年，美国在医疗保健上花费了127亿美元。

rows.s: Former Colorado governor Richard Lamm has been quoted as saying that the old and infirm "have a duty to die and get out of the way", so that younger, healthier people can realize their potential.
rows.zh: 据援引，前科罗拉多州州长理查德·拉姆曾说，老弱病残者有义务去死、让出位置，以便更年轻、更健康的人能实现他们的潜能。

rows.s: It is said that in England death is pressing, in Canada inevitable and in California optional. Small wonder.
rows.zh: 据说，在英国死亡是急迫之事，在加拿大是不可避免之事，而在加利福尼亚则是可有可无之事。难怪。

rows.s: I would not go that far.
rows.zh: 我不会说得那么极端。

rows.s: Energetic people now routinely work through their 60s and beyond, and remain dazzlingly productive.
rows.zh: 如今精力充沛的人通常会一直工作到60多岁甚至更晚，并保持惊人的工作效率。

rows.s: At 78, Viacom chairman Sumner Redstone jokingly claims to be 53.
rows.zh: 78岁的维亚康姆公司董事长萨姆纳·雷石东开玩笑说自己只有53岁。

rows.s: Americans' life expectancy has nearly doubled over the past century.
rows.zh: 在过去的一个世纪里，美国人的预期寿命几乎翻了一番。

rows.s: Supreme Court Justice Sandra Day O'Connor is in her 70 s, and former surgeon general C. Everett Koop chairs an Internet start-up in his 80 s.
rows.zh: 最高法院大法官桑德拉·戴·奥康纳已年逾70，而前卫生局局长C·埃弗里特·库普在80多岁时仍掌管着一家网络初创公司。

rows.s: These leaders are living proof that prevention works and that we can manage the health problems that come naturally with age.
rows.zh: 这些领导人就是活生生的证据，证明预防是有效的，而且我们能够应对随年龄自然出现的健康问题。

rows.s: As a mere 68-year-old, I wish to age as productively as they have.
rows.zh: 作为一个区区68岁的人，我希望能像他们那样高效率地变老。

rows.s: Yet there are limits to what a society can spend in this pursuit.
rows.zh: 然而，一个社会在这一追求上能投入的资源是有限度的。

rows.s: As a physician, I know the most costly and dramatic measures may be ineffective and painful.
rows.zh: 作为一名医生，我知道最昂贵、最激烈的手段可能既无效又痛苦。

rows.s: I also know that people in Japan and Sweden, countries that spend far less on medical care, have achieved longer, healthier lives than we have.
rows.zh: 我也知道，日本和瑞典——这两个在医疗上花费少得多的国家——的人们已经获得了比我们更长寿、更健康的生活。

rows.s: As a nation, we may be overfunding the quest for unlikely cures while underfunding research on humbler therapies that could improve people's lives.
rows.zh: 作为一个国家，我们可能在过度投资于对不大可能成功的疗法的追求，与此同时却对那些可能改善人们生活的更朴实疗法的研究投入不足。

rows.s: Failing hips can be replaced, clinical depression controlled, cataracts removed in a 30-minute surgical procedure.
rows.zh: 衰退的髋关节可以更换，临床抑郁症可以得到控制，白内障可以在一次30分钟的外科手术中摘除。

rows.s: Such advances offer the aging population a quality of life that was unimaginable when I entered medicine 50 years ago.
rows.zh: 这些进步为老龄化人口提供了一种我50年前从医时无法想象的生活质量。

rows.s: Physicians—frustrated by their inability to cure the disease and fearing loss of hope in the patient—too often offer aggressive treatment far beyond what is scientifically justified.
rows.zh: 医生们因无力治愈疾病而沮丧，又害怕患者丧失希望，于是常常提供远远超出科学合理范围的激进治疗。

rows.s: But not even a great health-care system can cure death—and our failure to confront that reality now threatens this greatness of ours.
rows.zh: 但即便是再好的医疗体系也无法治愈死亡——而我们无力正视这一现实，如今正威胁着我们这种伟大。

rows.s: Death is normal; we are genetically programmed to disintegrate and perish, even under ideal conditions.
rows.zh: 死亡是正常的；即使在理想条件下，我们在基因上也注定要走向衰败和死亡。

rows.s: We all understand that at some level, yet as medical consumers we treat death as a problem to be solved.
rows.zh: 在某种程度上我们都明白这一点，然而作为医疗消费者，我们却把死亡当作一个有待解决的问题来对待。

rows.s: Shielded by third-party payers from the cost of our care, we demand everything that can possibly be done for us, even if it's useless.
rows.zh: 由于有第三方付款者替我们承担医疗费用，我们便要求做一切可能为我们做的事，即便这些毫无用处。

rows.s: The most obvious example is late-stage cancer care.
rows.zh: 最明显的例子就是晚期癌症的治疗。

rows.s: Often it's the delivery which causes the audience to smile, so speak slowly and remember that a raised eyebrow or an unbelieving look may help to show that you are making a light-hearted remark.
rows.zh: 往往正是表达方式才使听众发笑，所以要慢慢地说，并且要记住，扬一下眉毛或露出一副不相信的神情，都可能有助于表明你是在说一句轻松的玩笑话。

rows.s: With other audiences you mustn't attempt to cut in with humor as they will resent an outsider making disparaging remarks about their canteen or their chairman.
rows.zh: 对于其他听众，你千万不可贸然插入幽默，因为他们会反感一个外人对他们的食堂或主席说三道四。

rows.s: If you intend using humor in your talk to make people smile, you must know how to identify shared experiences and problems.
rows.zh: 如果你想在谈话中用幽默来逗人发笑，你就必须懂得如何辨认大家共同的经历和问题。

rows.s: "Oh, that's God," came the reply, "but sometimes he thinks he's a doctor."
rows.zh: “哦，那是上帝，”回答传来，“但他有时自以为是个医生。”

rows.s: If you are part of the group which you are addressing, you will be in a position to know the experiences and problems which are common to all of you and it'll be appropriate for you to make a passing remark about the inedible canteen food or the chairman's notorious bad taste in ties.
rows.zh: 如果你是你所讲话的那个群体中的一员，你就能够了解你们大家所共有的经历和问题，而且你顺便评论一下难吃的食堂饭菜或主席糟糕透顶的领带品味，也是恰当的。

rows.s: You will be on safer ground if you stick to scapegoats like the Post Office or the telephone system.
rows.zh: 如果你坚持拿邮局或电话系统这类替罪羊开玩笑，你的处境就会更稳妥些。

rows.s: If you feel awkward being humorous, you must practice so that it becomes more natural.
rows.zh: 如果你觉得表现幽默很别扭，你就必须多加练习，以使其变得更自然。

rows.s: Include a few casual and apparently off-the-cuff remarks which you can deliver in a relaxed and unforced manner.
rows.zh: 加入一些随意而且看似即兴的话语，你可以用轻松而不做作的方式把它们说出来。

rows.s: Look for the humor.
rows.zh: 去寻找幽默。

rows.s: It often comes from the unexpected.
rows.zh: 它往往来自意想不到的地方。

rows.s: A twist on a familiar quote "If at first you don't succeed, give up" or a play on words or on a situation.
rows.zh: 对一句熟悉引语的曲解——“如果一开始你没有成功，那就放弃吧”——或是对文字、对某种情境的巧妙利用。

rows.s: Your humor must be relevant to the audience and should help to show them that you are one of them or that you understand their situation and are in sympathy with their point of view.
rows.zh: 你的幽默必须切合听众，并且应当有助于向他们表明你是他们中的一员，或者你理解他们的处境并赞同他们的观点。

rows.s: Search for exaggeration and understatement.
rows.zh: 去寻找夸张和轻描淡写之处。

rows.s: Look at your talk and pick out a few words or sentences which you can turn about and inject with humor.
rows.zh: 审视你的讲话，挑出几个你能加以改动并注入幽默的词或句子。

rows.s: Depending on whom you are addressing, the problems will be different.
rows.zh: 问题会因你的谈话对象不同而不同。

rows.s: If you are talking to a group of managers, you may refer to the disorganized methods of their secretaries; alternatively if you are addressing secretaries, you may want to comment on their disorganized bosses.
rows.zh: 如果你在对一群经理讲话，你可以提及他们的秘书做事杂乱无章的方法；或者，如果你是在对秘书们讲话，你也许会想评论他们杂乱无章的老板。

rows.s: Here is an example, which I heard at a nurses' convention, of a story which works well because the audience all shared the same view of doctors.
rows.zh: 这里有一个例子，是我在一次护士大会上听到的一个故事，这个故事效果很好，因为听众对医生都持有相同的看法。

rows.s: A man arrives in heaven and is being shown around by St. Peter.
rows.zh: 一个人来到天堂，正由圣彼得领着四处参观。

rows.s: He sees wonderful accommodations, beautiful gardens, sunny weather, and so on.
rows.zh: 他看到极好的住所、美丽的花园、晴朗的天气等等。

rows.s: Everyone is very peaceful, polite and friendly until, waiting in a line for lunch, the new arrival is suddenly pushed aside by a man in a white coat, who rushes to the head of the line, grabs his food and stomps over to a table by himself.
rows.zh: 每个人都非常平和、礼貌而友好，直到那位新来者在排队等候午餐时，突然被一个穿白大褂的人推到一边，那人冲到队伍前头，抓起食物，独自重步走到一张桌子旁。

rows.s: "Who is that?" the new arrival asked St. Peter.
rows.zh: “那是谁？”新来者问圣彼得。

rows.s: That compulsion has resulted in robotics—the science of conferring various human capabilities on machines.
rows.zh: 那种冲动催生了机器人技术——一门将人类的种种能力赋予机器的科学。

rows.s: And if scientists have yet to create the mechanical version of science fiction, they have begun to come close.
rows.zh: 如果说科学家尚未造出科幻作品中的那种机械产物，那么他们也已经开始接近这一目标了。

rows.s: As a result, the modern world is increasingly populated by intelligent gizmos whose presence we barely notice but whose universal existence has removed much human labor.
rows.zh: 结果，现代世界越来越多地被各种智能小玩意儿所充斥——我们几乎察觉不到它们的存在，但它们无处不在却减轻了大量的人力劳动。

rows.s: Our factories hum to the rhythm of robot assembly arms.
rows.zh: 我们的工厂和着机器人装配臂的节奏嗡嗡运转。

rows.s: Our banking is done at automated teller terminals that thank us with mechanical politeness for the transaction.
rows.zh: 我们的银行业务是在自动柜员机上办理的，这些机器会以机械式的礼貌为我们的每笔交易道谢。

rows.s: Our subway trains are controlled by tireless robot-drivers.
rows.zh: 我们的地铁列车由不知疲倦的机器人司机来控制。

rows.s: And thanks to the continual miniaturization of electronics and micro-mechanics, there are already robot systems that can perform some kinds of brain and bone surgery with submillimeter accuracy—far greater precision than highly skilled physicians can achieve with their hands alone.
rows.zh: 而且得益于电子设备和微观机械的不断微型化，目前已经出现了一些机器人系统，它们能以亚毫米级的精度实施某些脑部和骨骼手术——这种精度远远超过技艺高超的医生仅凭双手所能达到的水平。

rows.s: Since the dawn of human ingenuity, people have devised ever more cunning tools to cope with work that is dangerous, boring, burdensome, or just plain nasty.
rows.zh: 自从人类智慧萌发以来，人们就设计出越来越精巧的工具，用以应对那些危险、乏味、繁重或者干脆就令人厌恶的工作。

rows.s: But if robots are to reach the next stage of laborsaving utility, they will have to operate with less human supervision and be able to make at least a few decisions for themselves—goals that pose a real challenge.
rows.zh: 但是，如果机器人要达到节省人力效用的下一个阶段，它们就必须在更少的人为监督下运作，并且能够自行做出至少几个决定——而这些都是构成真正挑战的目标。

rows.s: Indeed the quest for true artificial intelligence has produced very mixed results.
rows.zh: 的确，对真正人工智能的探索所产生的结果好坏参半。

rows.s: Despite a spell of initial optimism in the 1960s and 1970s when it appeared that transistor circuits and microprocessors might be able to copy the action of the human brain by the year 2010, researchers lately have begun to extend that forecast by decades if not centuries.
rows.zh: 尽管在二十世纪六七十年代曾有过一阵最初的乐观——当时似乎晶体管电路和微处理器到2010年就有可能复制人脑的活动——但研究人员近来已经开始把这一预测推迟了数十年，乃至数百年。

rows.s: What they found, in attempting to model thought, is that the human brain's roughly one hundred billion nerve cells are much more talented—and human perception far more complicated—than previously imagined.
rows.zh: 他们在试图模拟思维的过程中发现，人脑那大约一千亿个神经细胞远比此前想象的更有本领，而人类的感知能力也远比此前想象的更为复杂。

rows.s: They have built robots that can recognize the error of a machine panel by a fraction of a millimeter in a controlled factory environment.
rows.zh: 他们已经造出了一些机器人，它们能够在受控的工厂环境中识别出机器面板上不到一毫米的误差。

rows.s: But the human mind can glimpse a rapidly changing scene and immediately disregard the 98 percent that is irrelevant, instantaneously focusing on the monkey at the side of a winding forest road or the single suspicious face in a big crowd.
rows.zh: 但人的大脑却能瞥一眼飞速变化的场景，立即忽略掉其中无关的那98%，同时即刻聚焦于蜿蜒林间小路旁的那只猴子，或一大群人中那张唯一可疑的面孔。

rows.s: The most advanced computer systems on Earth can't approach that kind of ability, and neuroscientists still don't know quite how we do it.
rows.zh: 地球上最先进的计算机系统都无法接近那种能力，而神经科学家们也仍然不太清楚我们究竟是如何做到这一点的。

rows.s: "While we know how to tell a robot to handle a specific error," says Dave Lavery, manager of a robotics program at NASA, "we can't yet give a robot enough 'common sense' to reliably interact with a dynamic world."
rows.zh: 美国宇航局某机器人项目负责人戴夫·拉弗里说：“尽管我们知道如何让机器人去处理某个具体的错误，但我们还无法赋予机器人足够的‘常识’，使其能够可靠地与一个不断变化的世界互动。”

rows.s: Both previous shocks resulted in double-digit inflation and global economic decline.
rows.zh: 此前两次石油危机都导致了两位数的通货膨胀和全球性的经济衰退。

rows.s: So where are the headlines warning of gloom and doom this time?
rows.zh: 那么，这次警示阴霾与厄运降临的头条新闻又在哪里呢？

rows.s: The oil price was given another push up this week when Iraq suspended oil exports.
rows.zh: 本周，由于伊拉克暂停石油出口，油价又被进一步推高。

rows.s: Strengthening economic growth, at the same time as winter grips the northern hemisphere, could push the price higher still in the short term.
rows.zh: 在冬季笼罩北半球的同时，不断增强的经济增长可能在短期内将油价推得更高。

rows.s: In most countries the cost of crude oil now accounts for a smaller share of the price of petrol than it did in the 1970s.
rows.zh: 在大多数国家，如今原油成本在汽油价格中所占的比重，比20世纪70年代时要小。

rows.s: Yet there are good reasons to expect the economic consequences now to be less severe than in the 1970s.
rows.zh: 然而，有充分的理由可以预期，如今的经济后果不会像20世纪70年代那样严重。

rows.s: Could the bad old days of economic decline be about to return?
rows.zh: 经济衰退那糟糕的旧时光会不会即将重现？

rows.s: In Europe, taxes account for up to four-fifths of the retail price, so even quite big changes in the price of crude have a more muted effect on pump prices than in the past.
rows.zh: 在欧洲，税收占到零售价格的五分之四之多，因此，即便原油价格出现相当大的波动，对加油站油价的影响也比过去更为微弱。

rows.s: Rich economies are also less dependent on oil than they were, and so less sensitive to swings in the oil price.
rows.zh: 富裕经济体对石油的依赖程度也比过去更低，因此对油价波动也不那么敏感了。

rows.s: That is less than one-quarter of the income loss in 1974 or 1980.
rows.zh: 这还不到1974年或1980年收入损失的四分之一。

rows.s: Energy conservation, a shift to other fuels and a decline in the importance of heavy, energy-intensive industries have reduced oil consumption.
rows.zh: 节约能源、转用其他燃料以及重型高耗能产业重要性的下降，都减少了石油的消耗。

rows.s: Software, consultancy and mobile telephones use far less oil than steel or car production.
rows.zh: 软件、咨询和移动电话所耗用的石油，远比钢铁或汽车生产要少。

rows.s: For each dollar of GDP (in constant prices) rich economies now use nearly 50% less oil than in 1973.
rows.zh: 按（不变价格计算的）每一美元GDP计算，富裕经济体如今使用的石油比1973年少了将近50%。

rows.s: The OECD estimates in its latest Economic Outlook that, if oil prices averaged $22 a barrel for a full year, compared with $13 in 1998, this would increase the oil import bill in rich economies by only 0.25-0.5% of GDP.
rows.zh: 经合组织在其最新一期的《经济展望》中估计，如果油价全年平均为每桶22美元（相比1998年的13美元），这只会使富裕经济体的石油进口费用增加相当于GDP的0.25%至0.5%。

rows.s: On the other hand, oil-importing emerging economies—to which heavy industry has shifted—have become more energy-intensive, and so could be more seriously squeezed.
rows.zh: 另一方面，重工业已转移至那些进口石油的新兴经济体，它们已变得更加能源密集，因此可能受到更严重的冲击。

rows.s: One more reason not to lose sleep over the rise in oil prices is that, unlike the rises in the 1970s, it has not occurred against the background of general commodity-price inflation and global excess demand.
rows.zh: 不必为油价上涨而焦虑的另一个理由是：与20世纪70年代的几次上涨不同，这次上涨并非发生在普遍的大宗商品价格通胀和全球需求过剩的背景之下。

rows.s: A sizable portion of the world is only just emerging from economic decline.
rows.zh: 世界上相当一部分地区才刚刚从经济衰退中走出来。

rows.s: Since OPEC agreed to supply-cuts in March, the price of crude oil has jumped to almost $26 a barrel, up from less than $10 last December.
rows.zh: 自从3月份欧佩克同意削减石油供应以来，原油价格已从去年12月的不足10美元跃升至每桶近26美元。

rows.s: The Economist's commodity price index is broadly unchanging from a year ago.
rows.zh: 《经济学人》的大宗商品价格指数与一年前相比大体上没有变化。

rows.s: In 1973 commodity prices jumped by 70%, and in 1979 by almost 30%.
rows.zh: 1973年商品价格上涨了70%，而1979年又上涨了将近30%。

rows.s: This near-tripling of oil prices calls up scary memories of the 1973 oil shock, when prices quadrupled, and 1979–1980, when they also almost tripled.
rows.zh: 这次油价近乎三倍的上涨，唤起了人们对1973年石油危机（当时油价上涨了三倍）以及1979至1980年（当时油价也几乎涨至三倍）的可怕记忆。

rows.s: Doctors have used that principle in recent years to justify using high doses of morphine to control terminally ill patients'pain, even though increasing dosages will eventually kill the patient.
rows.zh: 近年来，医生们一直用那条原则来为使用大剂量吗啡控制晚期病人疼痛的做法正名，尽管不断加大剂量最终会导致病人死亡。

rows.s: On another level, many in the medical community acknowledge that the assisted-suicide debate has been fueled in part by the despair of patients for whom modern medicine has prolonged the physical agony of dying.
rows.zh: 在另一个层面上，医学界许多人承认，协助自杀之争在一定程度上是被那些病人的绝望情绪所助长的——对这些病人而言，现代医学延长了他们临终时的肉体痛苦。

rows.s: If you're a physician, you can risk your patient's suicide as long as you don't intend their suicide."
rows.zh: 如果你是一名医生，只要你无意让病人自杀，你就可以冒病人自杀的风险。

rows.s: "We don't call those deaths homicides because the doctors didn't intend to kill their patients, although they risked their death.
rows.zh: 我们不把那些死亡称为他杀，因为医生并非有意杀死病人，尽管他们确实冒了使病人死亡的风险。

rows.s: "It's like surgery," he says.
rows.zh: 他说："这就像做手术。"

rows.s: George Annas, chair of the health law department at Boston University, maintains that, as long as a doctor prescribes a drug for a legitimate medical purpose, the doctor has done nothing illegal even if the patient uses the drug to hasten death.
rows.zh: 波士顿大学卫生法律系主任乔治·安纳斯坚持认为，只要医生是出于正当的医疗目的开药，那么即使病人用该药加速死亡，医生也没有任何违法之处。

rows.s: Nancy Dubler, director of Montefiore Medical Center, contends that the principle will shield doctors who "until now have very, very strongly insisted that they could not give patients sufficient medication to control their pain if that might hasten death".
rows.zh: 蒙特菲奥里医疗中心主任南希·杜布勒认为，该原则将保护那些医生——他们迄今一直极力坚称，如果足量用药可能加速死亡，他们就不能给病人这样的药物来控制疼痛。

rows.s: Although it ruled that there is no constitutional right to physician-assisted suicide, the Court in effect supported the medical principle of "double effect", a centuries-old moral principle holding that an action having two effects—a good one that is intended and a harmful one that is foreseen—is permissible if the actor intends only the good effect.
rows.zh: 尽管法院裁定宪法并未赋予医生协助自杀的权利，但最高法院实际上支持了"双重效应"这一医学原则——这是一条流传数百年的道德原则，它认为：一个具有两种效应的行为（一种是有意为之的好效应，一种是可预见的坏效应），只要行为者只意图实现其中好的效应，便是可以允许的。

rows.s: He says medical licensing boards "must make it clear... that painful deaths are presumptively ones that are incompetently managed and should result in license suspension".
rows.zh: 他说，医疗执照委员会"必须明确表态……痛苦的死亡可推定为处置不当所致，并应导致吊销行医执照"。

rows.s: "Large numbers of physicians seem unconcerned with the pain their patients are needlessly and predictably suffering", to the extent that it constitutes "systematic patient abuse".
rows.zh: "大量医生似乎对其病人正在不必要地且可预见地承受的疼痛漠不关心"，以至于这构成了"系统性的病人虐待"。

rows.s: Annas says lawyers can play a key role in insisting that these well-meaning medical initiatives translate into better care.
rows.zh: 安纳斯说，律师在坚持要求这些善意的医疗举措切实转化为更好的护理方面，能够发挥关键作用。

rows.s: The profession is taking steps to require young doctors to train in hospices, to test knowledge of aggressive pain management therapies, to develop a Medicare billing code for hospital-based care, and to develop new standards for assessing and treating pain at the end of life.
rows.zh: 医疗行业正在采取措施，要求年轻医生在临终关怀机构受训、考核积极疼痛管理疗法的知识、制定针对医院护理的医保收费代码，并制定临终疼痛评估与治疗的新标准。

rows.s: It identifies the undertreatment of pain and the aggressive use of "ineffectual and forced medical procedures that may prolong and even dishonor the period of dying" as the twin problems of end-of-life care.
rows.zh: 该报告把疼痛治疗不足和过度使用"可能延长甚至玷污临终阶段的无效而强制的医疗手段"确认为临终关怀的两大问题。

rows.s: Just three weeks before the Court's ruling on physician-assisted suicide, the National Academy of Science (NAS) released a two-volume report, Approaching Death: Improving Care at the End of Life.
rows.zh: 就在法院对医生协助自杀作出裁决前三周，美国国家科学院（NAS）发布了一份两卷本的报告——《走近死亡：改善临终关怀》。

rows.s: The Supreme Court's decisions on physician-assisted suicide carry important implications for how medicine seeks to relieve dying patients of pain and suffering.
rows.zh: 最高法院关于医生协助自杀的裁决，对于医学如何设法解除濒死病人的疼痛与折磨，具有重要的影响。

rows.s: Another was the growing professionalisation of scientific activity.
rows.zh: 另一个（发展）则是科学活动日益增长的职业化。

rows.s: No clear-cut distinction can be drawn between professionals and amateurs in science: exceptions can be found to any rule.
rows.zh: 在科学领域，无法在专业人士和业余爱好者之间划出清晰的界限：任何规则都能找到例外。

rows.s: Nevertheless, the word "amateur" does carry a connotation that the person concerned is not fully integrated into the scientific community and, in particular, may not fully share its values.
rows.zh: 然而，“业余爱好者”一词确实带有这样一种含义：即相关的人没有完全融入科学共同体，尤其是可能没有完全认同科学共同体的价值观。

rows.s: The growth of specialisation in the nineteenth century, with its consequent requirement of a longer, more complex training, implied greater problems for amateur participation in science.
rows.zh: 十九世纪专业化的发展，连同随之而来的对更长、更复杂训练的要求，意味着业余爱好者参与科学会面临更大的困难。

rows.s: The trend was naturally most obvious in those areas of science based especially on a mathematical or laboratory training, and can be illustrated in terms of the development of geology in the United Kingdom.
rows.zh: 这种趋势在那些尤其以数学或实验室训练为基础的科学领域中最为明显，并且可以通过英国地质学的发展加以说明。

rows.s: Specialisation can be seen as a response to the problem of an increasing accumulation of scientific knowledge.
rows.zh: 专业化可以被看作是对科学知识不断积累这一问题的一种应对。

rows.s: Thus, in the nineteenth century, local geological studies represented worthwhile research in their own right; but, in the twentieth century, local studies have increasingly become acceptable to professionals only if they incorporate, and reflect on, the wider geological picture.
rows.zh: 因此，在十九世纪，地方性地质研究本身就被视为有价值的研究；但到了二十世纪，地方性研究只有在纳入并反映更广阔的地质图景时，才越来越能被专业人士所接受。

rows.s: Amateurs, on the other hand, have continued to pursue local studies in the old way.
rows.zh: 另一方面，业余爱好者则一直以老办法继续从事地方性研究。

rows.s: A comparison of British geological publications over the last century and a half reveals not simply an increasing emphasis on the primacy of research, but also a changing definition of what constitutes an acceptable research paper.
rows.zh: 对过去一个半世纪英国地质学出版物的比较，不仅揭示出人们对研究首要地位日益重视，也揭示出关于何为合格研究论文这一定义的不断变化。

rows.s: As a logical consequence of this development, separate journals have now appeared aimed mainly towards either professional or amateur readership.
rows.zh: 作为这一发展的必然结果，如今出现了各自独立的期刊，它们主要面向专业读者或业余读者。

rows.s: A rather similar process of differentiation has led to professional geologists coming together nationally within one or two specific societies, whereas the amateurs have tended either to remain in local societies or to come together nationally in a different way.
rows.zh: 一个颇为相似的分化过程使专业地质学家在全国范围内聚集于一两个特定的学会之中，而业余爱好者则倾向于要么留在地方性学会，要么以另一种方式在全国范围内聚集。

rows.s: Although the process of professionalisation and specialisation was already well under way in British geology during the nineteenth century, its full consequences were thus delayed until the twentieth century.
rows.zh: 尽管职业化和专业化的进程在十九世纪的英国地质学中已经全面展开，但其全部影响却因此被推迟到了二十世纪。

rows.s: The overall result has been to make entrance to professional geological journals harder for amateurs, a result that has been reinforced by the widespread introduction of refereeing, first by national journals in the nineteenth century and then by several local geological journals in the twentieth century.
rows.zh: 总的结果是使业余爱好者更难进入专业地质期刊，这一结果又因评审制度的广泛引入而得到强化——先是十九世纪的全国性期刊引入评审，随后是二十世纪若干地方性地质期刊也引入了评审。

rows.s: In science generally, however, the nineteenth century must be reckoned as the crucial period for this change in the structure of science.
rows.zh: 然而，就整个科学而言，十九世纪必须被视为科学结构发生这一变化的关键时期。

rows.s: By splitting up the subject matter into smaller units, one man could continue to handle the information and use it as the basis for further research.
rows.zh: 通过把研究主题分割成更小的单元，一个人就能够继续处理这些信息，并把它作为进一步研究的基础。

rows.s: But specialisation was only one of a series of related developments in science affecting the process of communication.
rows.zh: 但专业化只是科学领域影响交流过程的一系列相关发展之一。

rows.s: And the Internet is not the only tool we have.
rows.zh: 而且互联网也不是我们拥有的唯一工具。

rows.s: Of course, the use of the Internet isn't the only way to defeat poverty.
rows.zh: 当然，使用互联网并非战胜贫困的唯一方法。

rows.s: And that is very good news because the Internet may well be the most powerful tool for combating world poverty that we've ever had.
rows.zh: 而这是个非常好的消息，因为互联网很可能是我们迄今为止拥有的对抗世界贫困的最强大工具。

rows.s: As a result, I now believe the digital divide will narrow rather than widen in the years ahead.
rows.zh: 因此，我现在相信，在未来几年里数字鸿沟会缩小而不是扩大。

rows.s: Within the next decade or two, one to two billion people on the planet will be netted together.
rows.zh: 在未来的十到二十年内，这个星球上将有十至二十亿人通过网络联结在一起。

rows.s: More and more governments, afraid their countries will be left behind, want to spread Internet access.
rows.zh: 越来越多的政府由于担心本国会被甩在后面，都想要普及互联网接入。

rows.s: As the Internet becomes more and more commercialized, it is in the interest of business to universalize access—after all, the more people online, the more potential customers there are.
rows.zh: 随着互联网日益商业化，普及网络接入符合商业利益——毕竟，上网的人越多，潜在的客户就越多。

rows.s: There are technological reasons to hope the digital divide will narrow.
rows.zh: 有一些技术上的理由让我们希望数字鸿沟会缩小。

rows.s: There are reasons to be optimistic.
rows.zh: 我们有理由感到乐观。

rows.s: What was less visible then, however, were the new, positive forces that work against the digital divide.
rows.zh: 然而，当时不太明显的，是那些对抗数字鸿沟的新的、积极的力量。

rows.s: My wife and I lectured about this looming danger twenty years ago.
rows.zh: 二十年前，我和妻子就曾就这一迫近的危险作过演讲。

rows.s: But it does mean recognizing how important they can be in building the energy and telecom infrastructures needed to take full advantage of the Internet.
rows.zh: 但它确实意味着要认识到，它们在建设充分利用互联网所需的能源和电信基础设施方面，能够发挥多么重要的作用。

rows.s: That doesn't mean lying down and becoming fooled, or letting foreign corporations run uncontrolled.
rows.zh: 那并不意味着甘愿屈服、受人愚弄，或听任外国公司不受控制地横行。

rows.s: The more foreign capital you have helping you build your Third Wave infrastructure, which today is an electronic infrastructure, the better off you're going to be.
rows.zh: 你拥有越多帮助你建设第三次浪潮基础设施（如今即电子基础设施）的外国资本，你的处境就会越好。

rows.s: I believe the same thing would be true in places like Brazil or anywhere else for that matter.
rows.zh: 我相信，在像巴西这样的地方，或者就此而言在任何其他地方，同样的情况也会成立。

rows.s: Immigrant Americans built them.
rows.zh: 移民到美国的人们建造了这些基础设施。

rows.s: They financed them.
rows.zh: 他们为这些基础设施提供资金。

rows.s: And that divide does exist today.
rows.zh: 而如今那种鸿沟确实存在。

rows.s: Guess who owns them now? The Americans.
rows.zh: 猜猜现在这些基础设施归谁所有？美国人。

rows.s: The English, the Germans, the Dutch and the French were investing in Britain's former colony.
rows.zh: 英国人、德国人、荷兰人和法国人都曾投资于英国昔日的殖民地（美国）。

rows.s: And that is why America's Second Wave infrastructure—including roads, harbors, highways, ports and so on—were built with foreign investment.
rows.zh: 这就是为什么美国的第二次浪潮基础设施——包括公路、港口、高速公路、码头等等——是用外国投资建成的。

rows.s: When the United States built its industrial infrastructure, it didn't have the capital to do so.
rows.zh: 当美国建设其工业基础设施时，它并没有这样做所需的资金。

rows.s: Countries that still think foreign investment is an invasion of their sovereignty might well study the history of infrastructure (the basic structural foundations of a society) in the United States.
rows.zh: 那些仍然认为外国投资是对其主权侵犯的国家，或许应该好好研究一下美国基础设施（即一个社会的基本结构性基础）的历史。

rows.s: A great deal of attention is being paid today to the so-called digital divide—the division of the world into the info (information) rich and the info poor.
rows.zh: 如今，人们正对所谓的数字鸿沟给予大量关注，即把世界划分为信息富有者和信息贫乏者。

rows.s: To take advantage of this tool, some impoverished countries will have to get over their outdated anti-colonial prejudices with respect to foreign investment.
rows.zh: 为了利用这一工具，一些贫困国家将不得不克服其在外国投资方面过时的反殖民偏见。

rows.s: But it has enormous potential.
rows.zh: 但它具有巨大的潜力。

rows.s: Then it sponsors lots of symposiums and a credibility project dedicated to wondering why customers are annoyed and fleeing in large numbers.
rows.zh: 接着，它又赞助了大量研讨会和一个可信度项目，专门用来探究顾客为何恼火并大量流失。

rows.s: Here is a troubled business that keeps hiring employees whose attitudes vastly annoy the customers.
rows.zh: 这是一个陷入困境的行业，它不断雇用那些态度极其惹恼顾客的员工。

rows.s: This is an explosive situation for any industry, particularly a declining one.
rows.zh: 对任何行业而言，这都是一种一触即发的危险局面，对一个正在衰落的行业来说尤其如此。

rows.s: The astonishing distrust of the news media isn't rooted in inaccuracy or poor reportorial skills but in the daily clash of world views between reporters and their readers.
rows.zh: 对新闻媒体这种惊人的不信任，其根源不在于报道失实或报道技巧拙劣，而在于记者与读者之间世界观的日常冲突。

rows.s: Reporters tend to be part of a broadly defined social and cultural elite, so their work tends to reflect the conventional values of this elite.
rows.zh: 记者往往属于一个广义上的社会文化精英阶层，因此他们的作品也往往反映这一精英阶层的传统价值观。

rows.s: Replies show that compared with other Americans, journalists are more likely to live in upscale neighborhoods, have maids, own Mercedeses, and trade stocks, and they're less likely to go to church, do volunteer work, or put down roots in community.
rows.zh: 回复表明，与其他美国人相比，记者更有可能住在高档社区、雇有女佣、开着奔驰、炒股，而较少去教堂、做志愿工作或在社区扎根。

rows.s: Then residents in these communities were phoned at random and asked the same questions.
rows.zh: 随后，这些社区的居民被随机打电话，并被问及同样的问题。

rows.s: Why do so many Americans distrust what they read in their newspapers?
rows.zh: 为什么如此多的美国人不信任他们在报纸上读到的东西呢？

rows.s: The organization is deep into a long self-analysis known as the journalism credibility project.
rows.zh: 该组织正深入开展一项被称为“新闻可信度项目”的长期自我剖析。

rows.s: In a recent survey, questionnaires were sent to reporters in five middle size cities around the country, plus one large metropolitan area.
rows.zh: 在最近一次调查中，问卷被寄给了全国五个中等城市以及一个大都市区的记者。

rows.s: There exists a social and cultural disconnect between journalists and their readers which helps explain why the "standard templates"of the newsroom seem alien to many readers.
rows.zh: 记者与读者之间存在一种社会和文化上的脱节，这有助于解释为什么新闻编辑室的“标准模板”在许多读者看来显得格格不入。

rows.s: In other words, there is a conventional story line in the newsroom culture that provides a backbone and a ready-made narrative structure for otherwise confusing news.
rows.zh: 换句话说，新闻编辑室文化中存在一条固定的故事主线，它为那些原本杂乱无章的新闻提供了主干和现成的叙事结构。

rows.s: Most journalists learn to see the world through a set of standard templates (patterns) into which they plug each day's events.
rows.zh: 大多数记者学会透过一套固定的模板（套路）来观察世界，并把每天发生的事件都套进这些模板中。

rows.s: But the sources of distrust go way deeper.
rows.zh: 但不信任的根源要深得多。

rows.s: Sad to say, this project has turned out to be mostly low-level findings about factual errors and spelling and grammar mistakes, combined with lots of head-scratching puzzlement about what in the world those readers really want.
rows.zh: 遗憾的是，这个项目最终得出的大多是些低层次的发现，涉及事实差错、拼写和语法错误，外加大量令人挠头的困惑——搞不清那些读者究竟想要什么。

rows.s: The American Society of Newspaper Editors is trying to answer this painful question.
rows.zh: 美国报纸编辑协会正试图回答这个令人痛苦的问题。

rows.s: If it did, it would open up its diversity program, now focused narrowly on race and gender, and look for reporters who differ broadly by outlook, values, education, and class.
rows.zh: 如果它真这么做，就会开放目前仅狭隘聚焦于种族和性别的多样化计划，去寻找那些在观念、价值观、教育和阶层上差异广泛的记者。

rows.s: But it never seems to get around to noticing the cultural and class biases that so many former buyers are complaining about.
rows.zh: 但它似乎从未抽出空来注意到那么多昔日读者正在抱怨的文化偏见和阶层偏见。

rows.s: In cars, too, concentration is increasing—witness Daimler and Chrysler, Renault and Nissan-but it does not appear that consumers are being hurt.
rows.zh: 在汽车业，集中程度同样在加剧——试看戴姆勒与克莱斯勒、雷诺与日产的合并——但消费者似乎并未因此受到损害。

rows.s: The mergers of telecom companies, such as WorldCom, hardly seem to bring higher prices for consumers or a reduction in the pace of technical progress.
rows.zh: 诸如世通公司之类的电信公司合并，似乎几乎不会给消费者带来更高的价格，也不会使技术进步的步伐放缓。

rows.s: Yet it is hard to imagine that the merger of a few oil firms today could re-create the same threats to competition that were feared nearly a century ago in the U.S., when the Standard Oil trust was broken up.
rows.zh: 然而，很难想象如今几家石油公司的合并会重新造成那些威胁，即大约一个世纪前在美国标准石油托拉斯被拆分时人们所担忧的对竞争的威胁。

rows.s: Examples of benefits or costs of the current concentration wave are scanty.
rows.zh: 有关当前集中浪潮所带来利益或代价的例子十分稀少。

rows.s: As productivity grows, the world's wealth increases.
rows.zh: 随着生产率的提高，世界的财富也随之增加。

rows.s: All these are beneficial, not detrimental, to consumers.
rows.zh: 所有这些对消费者都是有益的，而非有害的。

rows.s: I believe that the most important forces behind the massive M&A wave are the same that underlie the globalization process: falling transportation and communication costs, lower trade and investment barriers and enlarged markets that require enlarged operations capable of meeting customers' demands.
rows.zh: 我认为，推动这场大规模并购浪潮的最重要力量，与构成全球化进程基础的力量是相同的：即不断下降的运输和通信成本、不断降低的贸易和投资壁垒，以及要求扩大经营规模以满足顾客需求的扩大化市场。

rows.s: This phenomenon has created serious concerns over the role of smaller economic firms, of national businessmen and over the ultimate stability of the world economy.
rows.zh: 这一现象引发了人们对小型经济企业和本国企业家所起作用的严重担忧，也引发了对世界经济最终稳定性的严重担忧。

rows.s: The world is going through the biggest wave of mergers and acquisitions ever witnessed.
rows.zh: 世界正在经历一场有史以来规模最大的兼并与收购浪潮。

rows.s: Multinational corporations accounted for less than 20% of international trade in 1982.
rows.zh: 1982年，跨国公司在国际贸易中所占份额不足20%。

rows.s: There's no question that the big are getting bigger and more powerful.
rows.zh: 毫无疑问，大企业正变得越来越大、越来越强。

rows.s: Won't the wave of business concentration turn into an uncontrollable anti-competitive force?"
rows.zh: 商业集中的浪潮难道不会变成一股无法控制的反竞争力量吗？"

rows.s: Many in these countries are looking at this process and worrying: "
rows.zh: 这些国家中的许多人正注视着这一进程，并忧心忡忡地问道："

rows.s: And should one country take upon itself the role of "defending competition" on issues that affect many other nations, as in the U.S. vs. Microsoft case?
rows.zh: 在那些影响许多其他国家的问题上，一个国家是否应当像在美国诉微软案中那样，自行承担起"捍卫竞争"的角色呢？

rows.s: Won't multinationals shift production from one place to another when a nation gets too strict about infringements to fair competition?
rows.zh: 当某个国家对侵害公平竞争的行为管制过严时，跨国公司难道不会把生产从一地转移到另一地吗？

rows.s: Who is going to supervise, regulate and operate as lender of last resort with the gigantic banks that are being created?
rows.zh: 面对正在形成的这些巨型银行，谁来对其进行监管、调控，并充当其最后贷款人呢？

rows.s: A few weeks ago, Alan Greenspan warned against the megamergers in the banking industry.
rows.zh: 几周前，艾伦·格林斯潘对银行业的超大型合并提出了警告。

rows.s: The process sweeps from hyperactive America to Europe and reaches the emerging countries with unsurpassed might.
rows.zh: 这一进程从极度活跃的美国席卷至欧洲，并以无与伦比的威力抵达新兴国家。

rows.s: Yet the fact remains that the merger movement must be watched.
rows.zh: 然而，事实依然如此：并购运动必须受到密切关注。

rows.s: On the contrary, the price of communications is coming down fast.
rows.zh: 相反，通信价格正在迅速下降。

rows.s: In Argentina, for instance, after the reforms of the early 1990s, multinationals went from 43% to almost 70% of the industrial production of the 200 largest firms.
rows.zh: 以阿根廷为例，在20世纪90年代初的改革之后，跨国公司在200家最大企业的工业产值中所占比例从43%上升到了近70%。

rows.s: International affiliates account for a fast-growing segment of production in economies that open up and welcome foreign investment.
rows.zh: 在那些开放并欢迎外国投资的经济体中，国际子公司在生产中所占的份额正在快速增长。

rows.s: Today the figure is more than 25% and growing rapidly.
rows.zh: 如今这一数字已超过25%，并且还在迅速增长。

rows.s: For the women of my generation who were urged to keep juggling through the '80s, downshifting in the mid-'90s is not so much a search for the mythical good life—growing your own organic vegetables, and risking turning into one—as a personal recognition of your limitations.
rows.zh: 对于我这一代在整个80年代被敦促着不停连轴转的女性而言，90年代中期放慢生活节奏，与其说是去追寻那种神话般的美好生活——自己种有机蔬菜，甚至冒着自己也变成那种田园之人的风险——不如说是对自身能力局限的一种个人化认识。

rows.s: Downshifting—also known in America as "voluntary simplicity"—has, ironically, even bred a new area of what might be termed anti-consumerism.
rows.zh: 颇具讽刺意味的是，放慢生活节奏——在美国也被称为"自愿简朴"——甚至催生了一个或许可被称为反消费主义的新领域。

rows.s: When I decided to quit my full time employment it never occurred to me that I might become a part of a new international trend.
rows.zh: 当我决定辞去全职工作时，我从未想到自己可能会成为一种新的国际潮流的一部分。

rows.s: There are a number of best-selling downshifting self-help books for people who want to simplify their lives; there are newsletter's, such as The Tightwad Gazette, that give hundreds of thousands of Americans useful tips on anything from recycling their cling-film to making their own soap; there are even support groups for those who want to achieve the mid- '90s equivalent of dropping out.
rows.zh: 有许多畅销的、面向想简化生活之人的放慢节奏类自助书籍；有一些时事通讯，如《吝啬鬼公报》，它们就从回收保鲜膜到自制肥皂等各种事情向数十万美国人提供实用建议；甚至还有面向那些想实现90年代中期版"退出主流"之人的互助小组。

rows.s: In America, the move away from juggling to a simpler, less materialistic lifestyle is a well-established trend.
rows.zh: 在美国，从忙于应付生活转向更简单、不那么物质化的生活方式的这种转变，已是一种确立已久的趋势。

rows.s: Nothing could persuade me to return to the kind of life Kelsey used to advocate and I once enjoyed: 12-hour working days, pressured deadlines, the fearful strain of office politics and the limitations of being a parent on "quality time".
rows.zh: 没有什么能说服我回到凯尔西曾经鼓吹、我也曾经享受过的那种生活：每天工作12小时、压力重重的截止期限、办公室政治带来的可怕紧张，以及作为家长在"优质时间"上的种种限制。

rows.s: I have discovered, as perhaps Kelsey will after her much-publicized resignation from the editorship of She after a build-up of stress, that abandoning the doctrine of "juggling your life", and making the alternative move into "downshifting" brings with it far greater rewards than financial success and social status.
rows.zh: 我已经发现——也许凯尔西在因压力累积而备受关注地辞去《她》杂志主编一职后也会发现——放弃"忙于应付生活"的信条，转而选择"放慢生活节奏"，所带来的回报远远大于经济上的成功和社会地位。

rows.s: I have been transformed from a passionate advocate of the philosophy of "having it all", preached by Linda Kelsey for the past seven years in the pages of She magazine, into a woman who is happy to settle for a bit of everything.
rows.zh: 我已经从"拥有一切"这一理念的狂热拥护者——这一理念是琳达·凯尔西在过去七年里在《她》杂志上所宣扬的——转变成了一个乐于对每样事物都浅尝辄止、知足常乐的女人。

rows.s: Curiously, some two-and-a-half years and two novels later, my experiment in what the Americans term "downshifting"has turned my tired excuse into an absolute reality.
rows.zh: 奇怪的是，大约两年半、两部小说之后，我在美国人称之为"放慢生活节奏"方面的尝试，已经把我那陈腐的借口变成了不折不扣的现实。

rows.s: A lateral move that hurt my pride and blocked my professional progress prompted me to abandon my relatively high profile career although, in the manner of a disgraced government minister, I covered my exit by claiming "I wanted to spend more time with my family".
rows.zh: 一次伤害了我的自尊心、阻碍了我职业发展的平级调动，促使我放弃了相对高调的职业，尽管我像一位声名扫地的政府部长那样，通过声称"我想多花些时间陪伴家人"来掩饰自己的离职。

rows.s: While in America the trend started as a reaction to the economic decline—after the mass redundancies caused by downsizing in the late '80s—and is still linked to the politics of thrift, in Britain, at least among the middle-class downshifters of my acquaintance, we have different reasons for seeking to simplify our lives.
rows.zh: 虽然在美国，这一趋势始于对经济衰退的反应——出现在80年代末因精简机构而导致大规模裁员之后——且至今仍与节俭政治相关联，但在英国，至少在我所认识的中产阶级放慢节奏者中，我们想要简化生活的理由却各不相同。
